en301549-single-biometric.one: The product's content relies on one biometric characteristic, so people with motor disabilities or others who might not be able to use that biometric characteristic (like a fingerprint ID) may be blocked from accessing the content. This occurs on the following page(s):
en301549-single-biometric.multiple: The product's content relies on one biometric characteristic, so people with motor disabilities or others who might not be able to use that biometric characteristic (like a fingerprint ID) may be blocked from accessing the content. This occurs on the following page(s):
en301549-single-biometric.short: Content relies on one biometric characteristic

en301549-accessibility-info-not-preserve.one: The product's content does not preserve accessibility information when the content is converted from one format to another, so some information necessary to make portions of the content accessible is not provided in the new format, and this content may not be available to some people with disabilities. This occurs on the following page(s):
en301549-accessibility-info-not-preserve.multiple: The product's content does not preserve accessibility information when the content is converted from one format to another, so some information necessary to make portions of the content accessible is not provided in the new format, and this content may not be available to some people with disabilities. This occurs on the following page(s):
en301549-accessibility-info-not-preserve.short: Content does not preserve accessibility info

en301549-video-player-no-captions.one: A multimedia player cannot display closed captions, so people who are deaf are not able to access the dialogue and other information contained in the multimedia's audio track through synchronized text captions. This occurs on the following page(s):
en301549-video-player-no-captions.multiple: Multiple multimedia players cannot play closed captioning, so people who are deaf are not able to access the dialogue and other information contained in the multimedia's audio track through synchronized text captions. This occurs on the following page(s):
en301549-video-player-no-captions.short: Multimedia player cannot display closed captions

en301549-video-player-captions-not-sync.one: A multimedia player can display captions but they are not synchronized to the audio track, so people who are deaf, hard of hearing and others who rely on captions to understand the content, will miss the context of the information provided by the captions on the following page(s):
en301549-video-player-captions-not-sync.multiple: Multiple multimedia players can display captions but the captions are not synchronized to the audio track, so people who are deaf, hard of hearing and others who rely on captions to understand the content, will miss the context of the information provided by the captions on the following page(s):
en301549-video-player-captions-not-sync.short: Closed captions not synced with audio

en301549-video-app-captions-not-preserve.one: The product does not preserve caption data during transmitting, converting, or recording video, so some information necessary to make portions of the content accessible is not provided in the new format, and this content may not be available to some people with disabilities. This occurs on the following page(s):
en301549-video-app-captions-not-preserve.multiple: The product does not preserve caption data during transmitting, converting, or recording video, so some information necessary to make portions of the content accessible is not provided in the new format, and this content may not be available to some people with disabilities. This occurs on the following page(s):
en301549-video-app-captions-not-preserve.short: App does not preserve caption data

en301549-video-player-captions-not-adapt.one: A multimedia player does not provide a way for the user to modify the appearance of captions to their individual needs, so people who are deaf, have limited hearing, and others who rely on captions to understand the content may not have access to the information. This occurs on the following page(s):
en301549-video-player-captions-not-adapt.multiple: Multiple multimedia players do not provide a way for the user to modify the appearance of captions to their individual needs, so people who are deaf, have limited hearing, and others who rely on captions to understand the content may not have access to the information. This occurs on the following page(s):

en301549-video-player-subtitles-not-spok.one: A multimedia player that provides access to subtitles does not provide an option for the subtitles to be read aloud, so people who are blind or low vision may not be able to hear the dialogue in a language they can understand. This occurs on the following page(s):
en301549-video-player-subtitles-not-spok.multiple: Multiple multimedia players that provide access to subtitles do not provide an option for the subtitles to be read aloud, so people who are blind or low vision may not be able to hear the dialogue in a language they can understand. This occurs on the following page(s):

en301549-video-player-no-ad-track.one: A multimedia player cannot play an audio description track, so people who are blind or have low vision are not able to access the information in the video portion of the multimedia described in the audio track. This occurs on the following page(s):
en301549-video-player-no-ad-track.multiple: Multiple multimedia players cannot play an audio description track, so people who are blind or have low vision are not able to access the information in the video portion of the multimedia that is described in those audio tracks. This occurs on the following page(s):
en301549-video-player-no-ad-track.short: Multimedia player cannot play audio description

en301549-video-player-ad-track-not-sync.one: A multimedia player can play audio descriptions but the descriptions are not synchronized to the video, so people with disabilities who rely on audio description to understand the content, will miss context provided by the visual for the audio descriptions on the following page(s):
en301549-video-player-ad-track-not-sync.multiple: Multiple multimedia players can play audio descriptions but the descriptions are not synchronized to the video, so people with disabilities who rely on audio description to understand the content, will miss context provided by the visual for the audio descriptions on the following page(s):
en301549-video-player-ad-track-not-sync.short: Audio description not synced with video

en301549-video-app-ad-track-not-preserve.one: The application does not preserve the audio description and/or the audio description becomes unsynchronized to the video during transmitting, converting, or recording video. So, some information necessary to make portions of the content accessible is not provided in the new format, or the information becomes out of sync with the video, and this content may be missing context or missing altogether for some people with disabilities. This occurs on the following page(s):
en301549-video-app-ad-track-not-preserve.multiple: The application does not preserve the audio description and/or the audio description becomes unsynchronized to the video during transmitting, converting, or recording video. So, some information necessary to make portions of the content accessible is not provided in the new format, or the information becomes out of sync with the video, and this content may be missing context or missing altogether for some people with disabilities. This occurs on the following page(s):
en301549-video-app-ad-track-not-preserve.short: App does not preserve audio description data

en301549-video-player-ad-control-missing.one: A multimedia player provides a closed caption control but does not also provide a control to activate the audio description track, so people who are blind, low vision, and others who need audio description will not be able to access information provided by the video alone. This occurs on the following page(s):
en301549-video-player-ad-control-missing.multiple: Multiple multimedia players provide a closed caption control but do not also provide a control to activate the audio description track, so people who are blind, low vision, and others who need audio description will not be able to access information provided by the video alone. This occurs on the following page(s):

en301549-video-player-cc-ad-wrong-level.one: A multimedia player does not provide the controls for closed captions and audio descriptions at the same level as the other media controls, so people with disabilities who use closed captions and audio descriptions may be unable to find the controls to activate the closed captions and audio descriptions. This occurs on the following page(s):
en301549-video-player-cc-ad-wrong-level.multiple: Multiple multimedia players do not provide the controls for closed captions and audio descriptions at the same level as the other media controls, so people with disabilities who use closed captions and audio descriptions may be unable to find the controls to activate the closed captions and audio descriptions. This occurs on the following page(s):
en301549-video-player-cc-ad-wrong-level.short: CC and AD controls on wrong level

en301549-video-player-cc-wrong-level.one: A multimedia player does not provide the controls for closed captions at the same level as the other media controls, so people who are deaf, hard of hearing, and others who use closed captions may be unable to find the controls to activate the closed captions. This occurs on the following page(s):
en301549-video-player-cc-wrong-level.multiple: Multiple multimedia players do not provide the controls for closed captions at the same level as the other media controls, so people who are deaf, hard of hearing, and others who use closed captions may be unable to find the controls to activate the closed captions. This occurs on the following page(s):
en301549-video-player-cc-wrong-level.short: Closed caption control on wrong level

eu-wad-statement-missing.one: The product does not provide an accessibility statement, so people with disabilities will not be provided with information about the challenges they may face using the website or mobile application and will not be given a path to provide feedback on any accessibility barriers they may encounter or how to request accessible alternatives.
eu-wad-statement-missing.multiple: The product does not provide an accessibility statement, so people with disabilities will not be provided with information about the challenges they may face using the website or mobile application and will not be given a path to provide feedback on any accessibility barriers they may encounter or how to request accessible alternatives.

eu-wad-statement-missing-enforcement-con.one: The accessibility statement does not provide information on the enforcement of the requirements of the European Union’s Web Accessibility directive and who to contact (the enforcement body) if any accessibility issue or request for an accessible alternative is not successfully resolved through the feedback mechanism.
eu-wad-statement-missing-enforcement-con.multiple: The accessibility statement does not provide information on the enforcement of the requirements of the European Union’s Web Accessibility directive and who to contact (the enforcement body) if any accessibility issue or request for an accessible alternative is not successfully resolved through the feedback mechanism.
eu-wad-statement-missing-enforcement-con.short: Accessibility Statement is missing Enforcement content

eu-wad-statement-missing-feedback-conten.one: The product's accessibility statement does not provide feedback and contact information, so people with disabilities will not know what mechanism is available to provide feedback on any accessibility issues encountered, and will not know who to contact to share these issues.
eu-wad-statement-missing-feedback-conten.multiple: The product's accessibility statement does not provide feedback and contact information, so people with disabilities will not know what mechanism is available to provide feedback on any accessibility issues encountered, and will not know who to contact to share these issues.
eu-wad-statement-missing-feedback-conten.short: Accessibility Statement is missing Feedback content

eu-wad-statement-missing-general-content.one: The product’s accessibility statement is missing general information about the product’s accessibility compliance, including what content is not accessible, the overall commitment to accessibility, date of statement creation, the scope of the product’s content covered in the accessibility statement and other general information, so people with disabilities will not know what product content is covered by the accessibility statement, when it was created and reviewed, the accessibility compliance level of the product, and other general accessibility information related to the product.
eu-wad-statement-missing-general-content.multiple: The product’s accessibility statement is missing general information about the product’s accessibility compliance, including what content is not accessible, the overall commitment to accessibility, date of statement creation, the scope of the product’s content covered in the accessibility statement and other general information, so people with disabilities will not know what product content is covered by the accessibility statement, when it was created and reviewed, the accessibility compliance level of the product, and other general accessibility information related to the product.
eu-wad-statement-missing-general-content.short: Accessibility Statement is missing General Information content

eu-wad-statement-not-accessible.one: The product's accessibility statement does not conform to WCAG 2.1, so the accessibility statement and the information it contains will not be accessible to some people with disabilities.
eu-wad-statement-not-accessible.multiple: The product's accessibility statement does not conform to WCAG 2.1, so the accessibility statement and the information it contains will not be accessible to some people with disabilities.

eu-wad-statement-wrong-place-mobile.one: The product's accessibility statement is not available on the website or downloaded application, so people with disabilities will not know information about the accessibility compliance of the product or any mechanisms that might be available to provide feedback if any accessibility issues are encountered.
eu-wad-statement-wrong-place-mobile.multiple: The product's accessibility statement is not available on the website or downloaded application, so people with disabilities will not know information about the accessibility compliance of the product or any mechanisms that might be available to provide feedback if any accessibility issues are encountered.
eu-wad-statement-wrong-place-mobile.short: Accessibility Statement cannot be reached from the website or the app download

eu-wad-statement-wrong-place-web.one: The product's accessibility statement is not available on the website, so people with disabilities will not know information about the accessibility compliance of the product or any mechanisms that might be available to provide feedback if any accessibility issues are encountered.
eu-wad-statement-wrong-place-web.multiple: The product's accessibility statement is not available on the website, so people with disabilities will not know information about the accessibility compliance of the product or any mechanisms that might be available to provide feedback if any accessibility issues are encountered.
eu-wad-statement-wrong-place-web.short: Accessibility Statement cannot be reached from the website

eu-wad-feedback-missing.one: The accessibility statement does not provide a mechanism to provide feedback on the accessibility of the product, so people with disabilities will not be able to report any accessibility barriers they encounter or request accessible alternatives for content and/or workflows.
eu-wad-feedback-missing.multiple: The accessibility statement does not provide a mechanism to provide feedback on the accessibility of the product, so people with disabilities will not be able to report any accessibility barriers they encounter or request accessible alternatives for content and/or workflows.

area-alt.one: An image map element that also functions as a link or button does not have a text alternative, so people who are blind and/or use a screen reader will not be able to access the information available in that section of the image map, nor will they know they know the purpose of the link or button. This occurs on the following page(s):
area-alt.multiple: Multiple image map elements that also function as links or buttons do not have a text alternative, so people who are blind and/or use a screen reader will not be able to access the information available in those portions of the image map(s), nor will they know they know the purpose of the links or buttons. This occurs on the following page(s):
area-alt.short: Active <area> elements must have alternative text

aria-allowed-attr.one: An element has an invalid attribute in its HTML code that is intended to provide its programmatic role, name, state, or another property to assistive technology, so people who are blind and/or use a screen reader or other assistive technology may not be able to understand the name, purpose, or content of the element or how to interact with it. This occurs on the following page(s):
aria-allowed-attr.multiple: Multiple elements have an invalid attribute in its HTML code that is intended to provide its programmatic role, name, state, or another property to assistive technology, so people who are blind and/or use a screen reader or other assistive technology may not be able to understand the name, purpose, or content of each element or how to interact with it. This occurs on the following page(s):
aria-allowed-attr.short: Elements must only use supported ARIA attributes

aria-braille-equivalent.one: An element has an attribute to provide a name or description that is conveyed to braille displays, but there is not a corresponding programmatic name or description that will be conveyed to other assistive technology, so the name/description will not be available to people who use a screen reader or other assistive technology. This occurs on the following page(s):
aria-braille-equivalent.multiple: An element has an attribute to provide a name or description that is conveyed to braille displays, but there is not a corresponding programmatic name or description that will be conveyed to other assistive technology, so the name/description will not be available to people who use a screen reader or other assistive technology. This occurs on the following page(s):
aria-braille-equivalent.short: aria-braille attributes must have a non-braille equivalent

aria-command-name.one: An element with a "link," "button," or "menu item" role is missing or has an incorrect programmatic name, so people who are blind and/or use a screen reader or other assistive technology may not be able to determine the name of the element and may not understand its purpose or content or how to interact with it. This occurs on the following page(s):
aria-command-name.multiple: Multiple elements with a "link," "button," or "menu item" role are missing or has an incorrect programmatic name, so people who are blind and/or use a screen reader or other assistive technology may not be able to determine the name of each element and may not understand its purpose or content or how to interact with it. This occurs on the following page(s):
aria-command-name.short: ARIA commands must have an accessible name

aria-conditional-attr.one: An element has attributes in its HTML code that are not appropriate or allowed for its programmatic role, so people who are blind and/or use a screen reader or other assistive technology may not be able to understand the name, purpose, or content of the element or how to interact with it, or they may be unable to interact with it at all. This occurs on the following page(s):
aria-conditional-attr.multiple: Multiple elements have attributes in its HTML code that are not appropriate or allowed for their respective programmatic roles, so people who are blind and/or use a screen reader or other assistive technology may not be able to understand the name, purpose, or content of each element or how to interact with it, or they may be unable to interact with it at all. This occurs on the following page(s):
aria-conditional-attr.short: ARIA attributes must be used as specified for the element's role

aria-deprecated-role.one: An element has an invalid or deprecated attribute in its HTML code that is intended to provide its programmatic role to assistive technology, so people who are blind and/or use a screen reader or other assistive technology may not be able to understand the name, purpose, or content of the element or how to interact with it. This occurs on the following page(s):
aria-deprecated-role.multiple: Multiple elements have an invalid or deprecated attribute in their HTML code that is intended to provide its programmatic role to assistive technology, so people who are blind and/or use a screen reader or other assistive technology may not be able to understand the name, purpose, or content of each element or how to interact with it. This occurs on the following page(s):
aria-deprecated-role.short: Deprecated ARIA roles must not be used

aria-hidden-body.one: An aria-hidden="true" attribute is present on a page's <body> tag, so people who are blind and/or use a screen reader or other assistive technology will not be able to perceive or interact with the content within the page's body. This occurs on the following page(s):
aria-hidden-body.multiple: An aria-hidden="true" attribute is present on multiple pages' <body> tags, so people who are blind and/or use a screen reader or other assistive technology will not be able to perceive or interact with the content within each page's body. This occurs on the following page(s):
aria-hidden-body.short: aria-hidden="true" must not be present on the document body

aria-hidden-focus.one: An element that is focusable or contains one or more focusable elements is programmatically hidden, so people who use the keyboard to navigate, as well as people who are blind and/or use a screen reader or other assistive technology, will not be able to perceive or interact with the element. This occurs on the following page(s):
aria-hidden-focus.multiple: Elements that are focusable or contain one or more focusable elements are programmatically hidden, so people who use the keyboard to navigate, as well as people who are blind and/or use a screen reader or other assistive technology, will not be able to perceive or interact with the elements. This occurs on the following page(s):
aria-hidden-focus.short: ARIA hidden element must not be focusable or contain focusable elements

aria-input-field-name.one: A form input element does not have a programmatic name, so people who are blind and/or use a screen reader or other assistive technology may not be able to determine the name of the element and may not understand its purpose or how to interact with it. This occurs on the following page(s):
aria-input-field-name.multiple: Multiple form input elements do not have a programmatic name, so people who are blind and/or use a screen reader or other assistive technology may not be able to determine the name of each element and may not understand its purpose or how to interact with it. This occurs on the following page(s):
aria-input-field-name.short: ARIA input fields must have an accessible name

aria-meter-name.one: A meter element that provides a graphical display of a numeric value within a defined range does not have a programmatic name, so people who are blind and/or use a screen reader or other assistive technology may not be able to determine the name of the element and may not understand its purpose or value or how to interact with it. This occurs on the following page(s):
aria-meter-name.multiple: Multiple meter elements that provide a graphical display of a numeric value within a defined range do not have a programmatic name, so people who are blind and/or use a screen reader or other assistive technology may not be able to determine the name of each element and may not understand its purpose or value or how to interact with it. This occurs on the following page(s):
aria-meter-name.short: ARIA meter nodes must have an accessible name

aria-progressbar-name.one: A progress bar element does not have a programmatic name, so people who are blind and/or use a screen reader or other assistive technology may not be able to determine the name of the element and may not understand its purpose or the information it conveys. This occurs on the following page(s):
aria-progressbar-name.multiple: A progress bar element does not have a programmatic name, so people who are blind and/or use a screen reader or other assistive technology may not be able to determine the name of the element and may not understand its purpose or the information it conveys. This occurs on the following page(s):
aria-progressbar-name.short: ARIA progressbar nodes must have an accessible name

aria-prohibited-attr.one: An element has an invalid attribute in its HTML code that is intended to provide its programmatic role, name, state, or another property to assistive technology, so people who are blind and/or use a screen reader or other assistive technology may not be able to understand the name, purpose, or content of the element or how to interact with it. This occurs on the following page(s):
aria-prohibited-attr.multiple: Multiple elements have an invalid attribute in its HTML code that is intended to provide that element's programmatic role, name, state, or another property to assistive technology, so people who are blind and/or use a screen reader or other assistive technology may not be able to understand the name, purpose, or content of each element or how to interact with it. This occurs on the following page(s):
aria-prohibited-attr.short: Elements must only use permitted ARIA attributes

aria-required-attr.one: An element is missing one or more required attributes in its HTML code that would provide its programmatic role, name, state, or another property to assistive technology, so people who are blind and/or use a screen reader or other assistive technology may not be able to understand the name, purpose, or content of the element or how to interact with it. This occurs on the following page(s):
aria-required-attr.multiple: Multiple elements are missing one or more required attributes in their HTML code that would provide that element's programmatic role, name, state, or another property to assistive technology, so people who are blind and/or use a screen reader or other assistive technology may not be able to understand the name, purpose, or content of each element or how to interact with it. This occurs on the following page(s):
aria-required-attr.short: Required ARIA attributes must be provided

aria-required-children.one: An element's programmatic role requires one or more child element(s) but the child element(s) is/are missing, so people who are blind and/or use a screen reader or other assistive technology may not be able to understand the purpose or content of the element or its related content. This occurs on the following page(s):
aria-required-children.multiple: Multiple elements' programmatic role requires one or more child element(s) but the child element(s) is/are missing, so people who are blind and/or use a screen reader or other assistive technology may not be able to understand the purpose or content of the element or its related content. This occurs on the following page(s):
aria-required-children.short: Certain ARIA roles must contain particular children

aria-required-parent.one: An element's programmatic role requires that the element have a parent element, but the parent element is missing, so people who are blind and/or use a screen reader or other assistive technology may not be able to understand the purpose or content of the element without the context provided by the parent. This occurs on the following page(s):
aria-required-parent.multiple: Some elements' programmatic role requires that the element have a parent element, but the parent element is missing, so people who are blind and/or use a screen reader or other assistive technology may not be able to understand the purpose or content of the element without the context provided by the parent. This occurs on the following page(s):
aria-required-parent.short: Certain ARIA roles must be contained by particular parents

aria-roles.one: An element has an invalid attribute in its HTML code that is intended to provide its programmatic role to assistive technology, so people who are blind and/or use a screen reader or other assistive technology may not be able to understand the name, purpose, or content of the element or how to interact with it. This occurs on the following page(s):
aria-roles.multiple: Multiple elements have an invalid attribute in their HTML code that is intended to provide its programmatic role to assistive technology, so people who are blind and/or use a screen reader or other assistive technology may not be able to understand the name, purpose, or content of each element or how to interact with it. This occurs on the following page(s):
aria-roles.short: ARIA roles used must conform to valid values

aria-toggle-field-name.one: A radio button, checkbox, or switch element does not have a programmatic name, so people who are blind and/or use a screen reader or other assistive technology may not be able to determine the name of the element and may not understand its purpose or content or how to interact with it. This occurs on the following page(s):
aria-toggle-field-name.multiple: Multiple radio button, checkbox, or switch elements does not have a programmatic name, so people who are blind and/or use a screen reader or other assistive technology may not be able to determine the name of each element and may not understand its purpose or content or how to interact with it. This occurs on the following page(s):
aria-toggle-field-name.short: ARIA toggle fields must have an accessible name

aria-tooltip-name.one: A tooltip element does not have a programmatic name, so people who are blind and/or use a screen reader or other assistive technology may not be able to determine the name of the element and may not understand its purpose or the information it conveys. This occurs on the following page(s):
aria-tooltip-name.multiple: Multiple tooltip elements do not have a programmatic name, so people who are blind and/or use a screen reader or other assistive technology may not be able to determine the name of each element and may not understand its purpose or the information it conveys. This occurs on the following page(s):
aria-tooltip-name.short: ARIA tooltip nodes must have an accessible name

aria-valid-attr-value.one: An element has an invalid attribute in its HTML code that is intended to provide its programmatic role, name, state, or another property to assistive technology, so people who are blind and/or use a screen reader or other assistive technology may not be able to understand the name, purpose, or content of the element or how to interact with it. This occurs on the following page(s):
aria-valid-attr-value.multiple: Multiple elements have an invalid attribute in its HTML code that is intended to provide its programmatic role, name, state, or another property to assistive technology, so people who are blind and/or use a screen reader or other assistive technology may not be able to understand the name, purpose, or content of each element or how to interact with it. This occurs on the following page(s):
aria-valid-attr-value.short: ARIA attributes must conform to valid values

aria-valid-attr.one: An element has an invalid attribute in its HTML code that is intended to provide its programmatic role, name, state, or another property to assistive technology, so people who are blind and/or use a screen reader or other assistive technology may not be able to understand the name, purpose, or content of the element or how to interact with it. This occurs on the following page(s):
aria-valid-attr.multiple: Multiple elements have an invalid attribute in its HTML code that is intended to provide its programmatic role, name, state, or another property to assistive technology, so people who are blind and/or use a screen reader or other assistive technology may not be able to understand the name, purpose, or content of each element or how to interact with it. This occurs on the following page(s):
aria-valid-attr.short: ARIA attributes must conform to valid names

blink.one: A blink element is present, and the user cannot pause, stop, or hide the blinking content, so people who cannot read text quickly or track moving objects, have attention deficit disorders or other cognitive disabilities, or use a screen reader may not be able to read or understand the content. This occurs on the following page(s):
blink.multiple: Blink elements are present, and the user cannot pause, stop, or hide the blinking content, so people who cannot read text quickly or track moving objects, have attention deficit disorders or other cognitive disabilities, or use a screen reader may not be able to read or understand the content. This occurs on the following page(s):
blink.short: <blink> elements are deprecated and must not be used

button-name.one: A button does not have a programmatic name, so its name (such as "Submit" or "Cancel") is not conveyed to screen readers and other assistive technologies and will not be available to people who use those technologies. This occurs on the following page(s):
button-name.multiple: Multiple buttons do not have a programmatic name, so each button's name (such as "Submit" or "Cancel") is not conveyed to screen readers and other assistive technologies and will not be available to people who use those technologies. This occurs on the following page(s):

bypass.one: The page does not have at least one element or feature (like a skip link, heading structure, HTML5 sectioning elements, or ARIA landmarks) to allow a user to skip repeated content (such as main navigation), so people who use the keyboard to navigate content or use a screen reader must navigate through repeated content on every page. This occurs on the following page(s):
bypass.multiple: The page does not have at least one element or feature (like a skip link, heading structure, HTML5 sectioning elements, or ARIA landmarks) to allow a user to skip repeated content (such as main navigation), so people who use the keyboard to navigate content or use a screen reader must navigate through repeated content on every page. This occurs on the following page(s):
bypass.short: Page must have means to bypass repeated blocks

color-contrast.one: The color contrast ratio between text and its background is less than 4.5:1 (or less than 3:1 for large text), so people who are colorblind or have low vision may have difficulty reading the text. This occurs on the following page(s):
color-contrast.multiple: The color contrast ratio between text and its background is less than 4.5:1 (or less than 3:1 for large text), so people who are colorblind or have low vision may have difficulty reading the text. This occurs on the following page(s):
color-contrast.short: Elements must meet minimum color contrast ratio thresholds

definition-list.one: A description list is not marked up properly, so the structure of the list is not properly conveyed to assistive technologies and people who are blind and/or use a screen reader. This occurs on the following page(s):
definition-list.multiple: Some description lists are not marked up properly, so the structures of the lists are not properly conveyed to assistive technologies and people who are blind and/or use a screen reader. This occurs on the following page(s):
definition-list.short: <dl> elements must only directly contain properly-ordered <dt> and <dd> groups, <script>, <template> or <div> elements

dlitem.one: A description list is not marked up properly, so the structure of the list is not properly conveyed to assistive technologies and people who are blind and/or use a screen reader. This occurs on the following page(s):
dlitem.multiple: Some description lists are not marked up properly, so the structures of the lists are not properly conveyed to assistive technologies and people who are blind and/or use a screen reader. This occurs on the following page(s):
dlitem.short: <dt> and <dd> elements must be contained by a <dl>

document-title.one: The page does not have a programmatic title, so people who use a screen reader will not be able to identify the purpose of the page without reading the page content. This occurs on the following page(s):
document-title.multiple: The page does not have a programmatic title, so people who use a screen reader will not be able to identify the purpose of the page without reading the page content. This occurs on the following page(s):
document-title.short: <dt> and <dd> elements must be contained by a <dl>

duplicate-id-aria.one: An ID value that programmatically associates elements (such as a form field and its text label) is duplicated on the same page, so the elements may not be properly associated, and the element's name or functionality may be misrepresented to people who use a screen reader or other assistive technologies. This occurs on the following page(s):
duplicate-id-aria.multiple: ID values that programmatically associate elements (such as a form field and its text label) are duplicated on the same page, so those elements may not be properly associated, and each element's name or functionality may be misrepresented to people who use a screen reader or other assistive technologies. This occurs on the following page(s):
duplicate-id-aria.short: IDs used in ARIA and labels must be unique

form-field-multiple-labels.one: A form field has multiple elements that provide its programmatic label, so the field's name and purpose may not be accurately conveyed to people who use a screen reader and other assistive technologies. This occurs on the following page(s):
form-field-multiple-labels.multiple: A form field has multiple elements that provide its programmatic label, so the field's name and purpose may not be accurately conveyed to people who use a screen reader and other assistive technologies. This occurs on the following page(s):
form-field-multiple-labels.short: Form field must not have multiple label elements

frame-focusable-content.one: The containing element for a frame or iframe has a tabindex="-1" attribute that prevents any of the content within the frame from being accessed using keyboard navigation. This occurs on the following page(s):
frame-focusable-content.multiple: The containing element for a frame or iframe has a tabindex="-1" attribute that prevents any of the content within the frame from being accessed using keyboard navigation. This occurs on the following page(s):
frame-focusable-content.short: Frames with focusable content must not have tabindex=-1

frame-title-unique.one: An iframe's title is not unique - another iframe on the same page has the same title, so people who are blind and/or use a screen reader will not be able to distinguish between the 2 iframes without entering and exploring them. This occurs on the following page(s):
frame-title-unique.multiple: Multiple iframe titles are not unique - another iframe on the same page has the same title, so people who are blind and/or use a screen reader will not be able to distinguish between the iframes without entering and exploring them. This occurs on the following page(s):
frame-title-unique.short: Frames must have a unique title attribute

frame-title.one: An iframe does not have a programmatic title that is conveyed to assistive technology, so people who are blind and/or use a screen reader or other assistive technology may not be able to understand the purpose or content of the iframe without browsing its content. This occurs on the following page(s):
frame-title.multiple: Multiple iframes do not have a programmatic title that is conveyed to assistive technology, so people who are blind and/or use a screen reader or other assistive technology may not be able to understand the purpose or content of each iframe without browsing its content. This occurs on the following page(s):
frame-title.short: Frames must have an accessible name

html-has-lang.one: No language is programmatically assigned to a page, so screen readers may mispronounce content. This occurs on the following page(s):
html-has-lang.multiple: No language is programmatically assigned to a page, so screen readers may mispronounce content. This occurs on the following page(s):
html-has-lang.short: <html> element must have a lang attribute

html-lang-valid.one: The page does not have a valid language assigned, so screen readers may mispronounce content. This occurs on the following page(s):
html-lang-valid.multiple: The page does not have a valid language assigned, so screen readers may mispronounce content. This occurs on the following page(s):
html-lang-valid.short: <html> element must have a valid value for the lang attribute

html-xml-lang-mismatch.one: Two languages are programmatically assigned to a page, so screen readers may mispronounce content depending on which language they apply to the page. This occurs on the following page(s):
html-xml-lang-mismatch.multiple: Two languages are programmatically assigned to a page, so screen readers may mispronounce content depending on which language they apply to the page. This occurs on the following page(s):
html-xml-lang-mismatch.short: HTML elements with lang and xml:lang must have the same base language

image-alt.one: An image does not have a text alternative, so people who are blind and/or use a screen reader will not be able to access the information available in the image, and if it is an active image, will not understand its function. This occurs on the following page(s):
image-alt.multiple: Some images do not have a text alternative, so people who are blind and/or use a screen reader will not be able to access the information available in the image, and if it is an active image, will not understand its function. This occurs on the following page(s):

input-button-name.one: A button does not have a programmatic name, so its name (such as "Submit" or "Cancel") is not conveyed to screen readers and other assistive technologies and will not be available to people who use those technologies. This occurs on the following page(s):
input-button-name.multiple: Multiple buttons do not have a programmatic name, so each button's name (such as "Submit" or "Cancel") is not conveyed to screen readers and other assistive technologies and will not be available to people who use those technologies. This occurs on the following page(s):
input-button-name.short: Input buttons must have discernible text

input-image-alt.one: An image does not have a text alternative, so people who are blind and/or use a screen reader will not be able to access the information available in the image, and if it is an active image (such as a button), they will not understand its function. This occurs on the following page(s):
input-image-alt.multiple: Some images do not have a text alternative, so people who are blind and/or use a screen reader will not be able to access the information available in each image, and if it is an active image (such as a button), will not understand its function. This occurs on the following page(s):
input-image-alt.short: Image buttons must have alternative text

label.one: A form input element does not have a programmatic name, so people who are blind and/or use a screen reader or other assistive technology may not be able to determine the name of the element and may not understand its purpose or how to interact with it. This occurs on the following page(s):
label.multiple: Multiple form input elements do not have a programmatic name, so people who are blind and/or use a screen reader or other assistive technology may not be able to determine the name of each element and may not understand its purpose or how to interact with it. This occurs on the following page(s):

link-in-text-block.one: Color is the only visual method used to identify a link, and a link text's contrast ratio with the color of the surrounding text is less than 3:1, so people who are colorblind or have low vision may not be able to identify the link. This occurs on the following page(s):
link-in-text-block.multiple: Color is the only visual method used to identify a link, and a link text's contrast ratio with the color of the surrounding text is less than 3:1, so people who are colorblind or have low vision may not be able to identify the link. This occurs on the following page(s):
link-in-text-block.short: Links must be distinguishable without relying on color

link-name.one: A link does not have discernible text, so people who are blind and/or use a screen reader or other assistive technology may not be able to understand the destination or function of the link. This occurs on the following page(s):
link-name.multiple: Multiple links do not have discernible text, so people who are blind and/or use a screen reader or other assistive technology may not be able to understand the destination or function of each link. This occurs on the following page(s):

list.one: An HTML list element contains content that is visually presented as a part of the list, but the content's HTML coding does not include it programmatically in that list, so the structure of the list is not correctly conveyed to people who are blind and/or use a screen reader or other assistive technology. This occurs on the following page(s):
list.multiple: Some HTML lists contain elements in the code that are not allowed in a programmatic list, so the structure and/or content of each list is not correctly conveyed to people who are blind and/or use a screen reader or other assistive technology. This occurs on the following page(s):
list.short: <ul> and <ol> must only directly contain <li>, <script> or <template> elements

listitem.one: Content that is visually presented as a list is not properly marked up as a list, so the structure of the list is not correctly conveyed to assistive technologies and people who are blind and/or use a screen reader. This occurs on the following page(s):
listitem.multiple: Some content that is visually presented as a list is not properly marked up as a list, so the structures of those lists are not correctly conveyed to assistive technologies and people who are blind and/or use a screen reader. This occurs on the following page(s):
listitem.short: <li> elements must be contained in a <ul> or <ol>

marquee.one: A marquee element is used to create a scrolling area of text.  However, the <marquee> tag is deprecated, so the text may not be rendered properly by a browser, and all users, including people who use assistive technology, may not be able to read or understand the content. This occurs on the following page(s):
marquee.multiple: A marquee element is used to create a scrolling area of text.  However, the <marquee> tag is deprecated, so the text may not be rendered properly by a browser, and all users, including people who use assistive technology, may not be able to read or understand the content. This occurs on the following page(s):
marquee.short: <marquee> elements are deprecated and must not be used

meta-refresh.one: A page is set to automatically refresh in intervals of less than 20 hours, so people with cognitive disabilities and people who use the keyboard to navigate content (including screen reader users) may become disoriented by unexpected refreshes. This occurs on the following page(s):
meta-refresh.multiple: A page is set to automatically refresh in intervals of less than 20 hours, so people with cognitive disabilities and people who use the keyboard to navigate content (including screen reader users) may become disoriented unexpectedly refreshes. This occurs on the following page(s):
meta-refresh.short: Delayed refresh under 20 hours must not be used

meta-viewport.one: The ability to zoom or scale the screen has been disabled, so people who have low vision and need to enlarge text to read it cannot do so. This occurs on the following page(s):
meta-viewport.multiple: The ability to zoom or scale the screen has been disabled, so people who have low vision and need to enlarge text to read it cannot do so. This occurs on the following page(s):
meta-viewport.short: Zooming and scaling must not be disabled

nested-interactive.one: The HTML code for a link or button is nested inside the code of another link or button, so assistive technologies may not be able to determine the function of the element. This occurs on the following page(s):
nested-interactive.multiple: The HTML code for a link or button is nested inside the code of another link or button, so assistive technologies may not be able to determine the function of the element. This occurs on the following page(s):
nested-interactive.short: Interactive controls must not be nested

no-autoplay-audio.one: Audio or video elements start playing automatically, so people who use a screen reader may be unable to understand the screen reader's speech output. This occurs on the following page(s):
no-autoplay-audio.multiple: Audio or video elements start playing automatically, so people who use a screen reader may be unable to understand the screen reader's speech output. This occurs on the following page(s):
no-autoplay-audio.short: <video> or <audio> elements must not play automatically

object-alt.one: An object used to embed multimedia (audio, video, applets, etc.) or another web page into the page does not have a programmatic name, so its content is not conveyed to screen readers and other assistive technologies and will not be available to people who use those technologies. This occurs on the following page(s):
object-alt.multiple: An object used to embed multimedia (audio, video, applets, etc.) or another web page into the page does not have a programmatic name, so its content is not conveyed to screen readers and other assistive technologies and will not be available to people who use those technologies. This occurs on the following page(s):

role-img-alt.one: An image does not have a text alternative, so people who are blind and/or use a screen reader will not be able to access the information available in the image, and if it is an active image, will not understand its function. This occurs on the following page(s):
role-img-alt.multiple: An image does not have a text alternative, so people who are blind and/or use a screen reader will not be able to access the information available in the image, and if it is an active image, will not understand its function. This occurs on the following page(s):
role-img-alt.short: [role="img"] elements must have an alternative text

scrollable-region-focusable.one: The content in a scrollable region cannot be accessed using a keyboard, so people who use a keyboard to navigate will not be able to view this content. This occurs on the following page(s):
scrollable-region-focusable.multiple: The content in a scrollable region cannot be accessed using a keyboard, so people who use a keyboard to navigate will not be able to view this content. This occurs on the following page(s):
scrollable-region-focusable.short: Scrollable region must have keyboard access

select-name.one: A select element does not have a programmatic name, so people who are blind and/or use a screen reader or other assistive technology may not be able to understand the purpose of the select control. This occurs on the following screen(s):
select-name.multiple: A select element does not have a programmatic name, so people who are blind and/or use a screen reader or other assistive technology may not be able to understand the purpose of the select control. This occurs on the following screen(s):
select-name.short: Select element must have an accessible name

server-side-image-map.one: A server-side image map is present on the page, and it is not accessible using keyboard navigation, so people who use keyboard navigation, including screen reader users, cannot access the content or functionality of the map. This occurs on the following page(s):
server-side-image-map.multiple: A server-side image map is present on the page, and it is not accessible using keyboard navigation, so people who use keyboard navigation, including screen reader users, cannot access the content or functionality of the map. This occurs on the following page(s):
server-side-image-map.short: Server-side image maps must not be used

svg-img-alt.one: An image does not have a text alternative, so people who are blind and/or use a screen reader will not be able to access the information available in the image, and if it is an active image, will not understand its function. This occurs on the following page(s):
svg-img-alt.multiple: An image does not have a text alternative, so people who are blind and/or use a screen reader will not be able to access the information available in the image, and if it is an active image, will not understand its function. This occurs on the following page(s):
svg-img-alt.short: <svg> elements with an img role must have an alternative text

td-headers-attr.one: Data is arranged visually like a complex data table with multiple rows of column headers and/or columns of row headers, but the data cells are incorrectly marked up and not associated with the appropriate headers, so people who are blind and/or use a screen reader will not be aware of the association between the table headers and their related data. This occurs on the following page(s):
td-headers-attr.multiple: Data is arranged visually like a complex data table with multiple rows of column headers and/or columns of row headers, but the data cells are incorrectly marked up and not associated with the appropriate headers, so people who are blind and/or use a screen reader will not be aware of the association between the table headers and their related data. This occurs on the following page(s):
td-headers-attr.short: Table cells that use the headers attribute must only refer to cells in the same table

th-has-data-cells.one: Data is arranged visually like a data table, but the table does not have proper markup for the table headers, so people who are blind and/or use a screen reader will not be aware of the association between the table headers and their related data. This occurs on the following page(s):
th-has-data-cells.multiple: Data is arranged visually like a data table, but the table does not have proper markup for the table headers, so people who are blind and/or use a screen reader will not be aware of the association between the table headers and their related data. This occurs on the following page(s):
th-has-data-cells.short: Table headers in a data table must refer to data cells

valid-lang.one: The page does not have a valid language assigned, so screen readers may mispronounce content. This occurs on the following page(s):
valid-lang.multiple: Multiple pages do not have a valid language assigned, so screen readers may mispronounce content. This occurs on the following page(s):
valid-lang.short: lang attribute must have a valid value

video-caption.one: Captions are not provided for media that includes audio and video, so the information provided by the audio track is not available to people who are deaf or hard of hearing. This occurs on the following page(s):
video-caption.multiple: Captions are not provided for media that includes audio and video, so the information provided by the audio track is not available to people who are deaf or hard of hearing. This occurs on the following page(s):

autocomplete-valid.one: The programmatic purpose provided for an input element (like a text input field) is not provided or not accurate, so information automatically suggested by the browser or assistive technology to fill in the input will be incorrect if it is present at all. This occurs on the following page(s):
autocomplete-valid.multiple: The programmatic purpose provided for an input element (like a text input field) is not provided or not accurate, so information automatically suggested by the browser or assistive technology to fill in the input will be incorrect if it is present at all. This occurs on the following page(s):
autocomplete-valid.short: autocomplete attribute must be used correctly

avoid-inline-spacing.one: When text spacing is adjusted to help people with vision, reading, and/or cognitive disabilities, the spacing for some or all text on the page does not adjust. This occurs on the following page(s):
avoid-inline-spacing.multiple: When text spacing is adjusted to help people with vision, reading, and/or cognitive disabilities, the spacing for some or all text on the page does not adjust. This occurs on the following page(s):
avoid-inline-spacing.short: Inline text spacing must be adjustable with custom stylesheets

target-size.one: A target's hit area does not meet a minimum 24x24 pixel size or spacing. making it difficult for users with hand tremors and those who have difficulty with fine motor movement to activate them accurately on the following page(s):
target-size.multiple: Multiple target hit areas do not meet a minimum 24x24 pixel size or spacing. making it difficult for users with hand tremors and those who have difficulty with fine motor movement to activate them accurately on the following page(s):
target-size.short: All touch targets must be 24px large, or leave sufficient space
